posts.title: 2 Chronicles 32:25
posts.excerpt: The same king I just held up as an example became proud. The same king who pursued God with his whole heart did not respond appropriately to the kindness God had shown him.

posts.title: 2 Chronicles 32:31
posts.excerpt: God withdrew from Hezekiah in order to test him and to see what was really in his heart. Sometimes the test is not in the storm. Sometimes the test is in the spotlight.

posts.title: 2 Chronicles 33:13
posts.excerpt: Manasseh was as far from God as a person could get. And then he prayed. And God heard him. If God could hear Manasseh in a Babylonian prison, He can hear your person too.

posts.title: Marry Someone Who Loves Jesus
posts.excerpt: On the surface this verse sounds harsh. But it was never about race. It was always about faith. And it is still relevant today.

posts.title: Do We Still Blush?
posts.excerpt: Ezra blushed in front of God. Most of us have gotten so good at managing the appearance of being okay that we forget what conviction even feels like.

posts.title: He Did Not Even Pray
posts.excerpt: Same Asa who once cried out to God against an army of a million. Now he is sick and does not even pray. The progression is sobering.

posts.title: 2 Chronicles 20:15
posts.excerpt: We default to fighting. Strategizing. Hustling. But sometimes God says sit down, watch, and let Me handle this one. Those might be the hardest seasons to obey.

posts.title: 2 Chronicles 22:12
posts.excerpt: Athaliah ruled for six years thinking she had wiped out the royal line. She had not. There was a boy in the temple. And he was the rightful king.

posts.title: The Gospel Hiding in the Law
posts.excerpt: Tucked into a chapter about a king and his enemies is one of the clearest pictures of the gospel I have ever seen.

posts.title: What Rises in Pride
posts.excerpt: What we see playing out in our culture today is not new. King Uzziah was the same story. Power. Pride. A line crossed. A public collapse.

posts.title: Careful
posts.excerpt: Jotham was the son of a king who fell in pride. He took the good of his father's life and left the bad. We can too.

posts.title: Highlighted: 2 Chronicles 28:23
posts.excerpt: He looked at the army that just destroyed him and thought their gods must be working. So he sacrificed to the gods of his enemies. And it led to his ruin.

posts.title: Highlighted: 2 Chronicles 31:1
posts.excerpt: They did not just go home and get back to their normal life. They left the festival and went to every town they could reach, and they tore down idols.

posts.title: Pray Before You Speak
posts.excerpt: Before he was the man who rebuilt a city, Nehemiah was a cupbearer who knew how to pause and pray in the middle of a sentence.

posts.title: The Gracious Hand of God
posts.excerpt: Nehemiah could have walked out of that throne room patting himself on the back. Instead he walked out with his eyes on the One who had been moving in the background.

posts.title: Remember Me
posts.excerpt: We all want to be seen. We all want our quiet faithfulness to count for something. Nehemiah just asked it of the only One who actually sees.

posts.title: 5 Signs You're Consuming Christian Content Instead of Actually Growing
posts.excerpt: A lot of us are consuming more than we ever have and growing less than we ever have. And the scary part is we do not always know the difference.

posts.title: When Fear Wears a Friendly Face
posts.excerpt: It is one thing when the bad guys are clearly the bad guys. It is harder when someone you trusted leans on your fear to push you out of obedience.

posts.title: They Read It and Went and Did It
posts.excerpt: They studied the Word, saw something they had been missing, and went and did it. No committee. No five-year plan. They just went.

posts.title: Write the Notes
posts.excerpt: It wasn't a huge thing. It wasn't complicated. But almost immediately, I started coming up with reasons why I didn't need to do it.
